# kkp_cluster_service_account (Resource)

A Kubernetes service account in a user cluster, created through the KKP API like the Service Accounts tab of the KKP dashboard, with cluster role bindings and a kubeconfig that uses its token. It works where admin kubeconfigs are disabled and the cluster has no OIDC. The kubeconfig ends up in state, so treat the state as a secret. The cluster must be up: create it after the `kkp_cluster`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "kkp_cluster_service_account" "ci" {
  cluster_id    = kkp_cluster.staging.id
  name          = "ci"
  cluster_roles = ["cluster-admin"]
}

provider "kubernetes" {
  config_path = local_sensitive_file.kubeconfig.filename
}

resource "local_sensitive_file" "kubeconfig" {
  content  = kkp_cluster_service_account.ci.kubeconfig
  filename = "${path.module}/ci.kubeconfig"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `cluster_id` (String) Cluster ID (`kkp_cluster.id`).
- `name` (String) Service account name, a DNS label.

### Optional

- `cluster_roles` (Set of String) Cluster roles to bind the service account to, e.g. `["cluster-admin"]`. KKP manages bindings for `cluster-admin`, `edit` and `view`, and for cluster roles labelled `component=userClusterRole`. Changes are made in place.
- `namespace` (String) Namespace of the service account. It must exist. Defaults to `kube-system`.
- `project_id` (String) Project ID. Defaults to the provider's `project_id`.

### Read-Only

- `creation_timestamp` (String)
- `id` (String) `<namespace>/<name>`.
- `kubeconfig` (String, Sensitive) Kubeconfig YAML with the service account's token, for the `kubernetes` and `helm` providers or `kubectl`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
tofu import kkp_cluster_service_account.ci <project_id>/<cluster_id>/<namespace>/<name>
```
